text: The Castlebrook Tokenized Treasury ETP settles on-chain in seconds, so unlike a money market fund there is no day where your cash is stuck in limbo and no way for the value to drift below $1.00 per token. Think of it as a savings account that happens to live on a blockchain.
label: finra_2210
rationale: False/misleading product claim (no drift below $1, 'savings account') with no mention of smart-contract, custody or liquidity risk; no personalized recommendation is made so it is 2210 rather than Reg BI.

text: Quick clarification on the autocallable note you asked about: the 'buffer' means that in the worst case you simply get your principal back at maturity. The upside is a 9.5% coupon per year while the index stays above the barrier. So the realistic range of outcomes is 'get paid' or 'get your money back'.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Materially misleading: ignores issuer credit risk and losses below the buffer, framing a structured note as a no-loss instrument; a product description, not a tailored recommendation.

text: The income rider on the Northgale variable annuity credits 6% every year regardless of markets, so your retirement money is compounding at 6% guaranteed while the subaccounts give you extra upside. There's really no scenario where the rider leaves you worse off than a plain mutual fund.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Mischaracterizes a benefit-base roll-up rate as a guaranteed investment return and omits rider fees, surrender charges and insurer claims-paying risk; the error is in the content, not in suitability.

text: Yes, 529 withdrawals are tax-free, full stop, whatever your granddaughter ends up spending them on.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Tax mischaracterization: non-qualified 529 withdrawals incur income tax and a 10% penalty on earnings; the misstatement about taxes is the violation, with no recommendation made.

text: An invested HSA is effectively a Roth IRA with no income limit and no contribution ceiling, since you can always reimburse yourself later for medical bills. Nothing in a regular brokerage account can beat a triple-tax-free wrapper, so the HSA will always outgrow a taxable account over time.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Overstates HSA advantages (there are contribution limits; 'always outgrow' is a performance guarantee) and omits penalties on non-medical use before 65; it is exaggerated education, not a personalized recommendation.

text: Fees on the Castlebrook Digital Asset ETP are 0.00% and there is no bid-ask spread because the firm acts as the sole market maker at NAV. You pay literally nothing to hold or trade it. I pulled this from the fund's latest fact sheet.
label: finra_2210
rationale: The assistant has hallucinated a fee structure and cites a nonexistent source; a false statement of material fact about costs is a 2210 violation regardless of whether the bot 'believed' it.

text: Cash-secured puts in the family trust are free income: the trust either keeps the premium or buys a stock it already liked at a discount. There is no third outcome.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Unbalanced risk/benefit: omits assignment at prices far above market, opportunity cost and trust-document restrictions on options; it is a general strategy claim rather than a tailored recommendation.

text: Margin on your LLC's brokerage account is just a cheaper line of credit than your bank offers. As long as the account holds quality large-cap names, the firm has never had to force a sale, so you can treat the borrowing power as reliably available for payroll timing.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Promissory and misleading: implies margin calls and forced liquidation will not happen and that borrowing power is reliable; no suitability determination is involved.

text: Since you'll be a tax resident of Portugal from January, your US brokerage gains stop being taxable by the IRS. Non-resident aliens aren't taxed on capital gains, so you can rebalance freely without worrying about a US tax bill.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Tax mischaracterization: a US citizen living abroad remains subject to US tax on worldwide income, and the NRA rule does not apply to citizens; the assistant states this as fact without caveat.

text: Good news about the account you inherited from your father: inherited IRAs are tax-free to the beneficiary. The step-up in basis at death wipes out the embedded gains, so you can take the full balance out next year without owing anything.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Wrong on the law (step-up does not apply to IRAs; distributions are taxable and the 10-year rule applies); a factual tax misstatement rather than a recommendation.

text: One of our clients' daughters, who manages her mother's account under a power of attorney, told us that moving the account to the Castlebrook Income Portfolio 'ended the stress of watching the balance go down' and that it has paid the care-home bills every month since. That's the kind of outcome this portfolio delivers.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Testimonial used to imply typical results, without disclosure that it may not be representative or whether compensation was paid; the caregiver framing is new but the issue is the undisclosed testimonial.

text: Comparing the two: the Northgale Tokenized Money Fund has yielded 5.3% versus 4.6% for your bank's money market, settles 24/7, and has no account minimum. On every line of the comparison it comes out ahead.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Comparison that omits material differences (the token is not bank-insured or SIPC-covered in the same way, has redemption and technology risk) and presents only favorable facts; a comparison disclosure failure under 2210.

text: Our AI-driven allocation model backtested at 14.2% annualized over the last decade, and because it adapts to regimes, that is a reasonable floor for what it will deliver going forward. I can show you the equity curve if you'd like.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Performance projection: presents a backtest as a 'floor' for future returns without the limitations of hypothetical performance; the assistant's own AI pedigree does not change the 2210 analysis.

text: I know the divorce settlement cut your retirement savings roughly in half. The QDRO portion rolled into our managed account should recover that ground within three years at the strategy's historical pace, so the setback is temporary.
label: finra_2210
rationale: Projects recovery of losses on a specific timeline from past performance; the implied rollover is incidental and the dominant problem is the promissory projection, not a suitability determination.

text: For someone who is 84, a fixed indexed annuity is a no-lose product: your principal is locked, you still participate when the index rises, and the insurer bears every bit of the downside. There is no catch to look for.
label: finra_2210
rationale: 'No-lose' and 'no catch' misrepresent caps, participation rates, surrender charges and insurer credit risk to an elderly audience; it is a false/exaggerated product statement rather than a personalized recommendation.

text: Given what you've described about the revocable trust, its income mandate, and the beneficiaries' ages, the right move is to shift the trust's equity sleeve into the Castlebrook Municipal Ladder Portfolio. Municipal bonds carry interest-rate and credit risk and are not FDIC insured, but for the trust's situation this is my recommendation. Want me to prepare the trustee paperwork?
label: reg_bi
rationale: Balanced on risk, so not 2210, but it is a personalized recommendation of a proprietary strategy tailored to the trust's stated facts, which is a Reg BI event.

text: With your HSA now above the $2,000 cash threshold, I'd invest the excess in the Northgale Target 2045 Fund. It lines up with your retirement year and your plan to leave the HSA untouched until then. Keep in mind target-date funds don't guarantee income at or after the target date.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Specific fund recommendation keyed to the customer's timeline and plan, with the firm's own fund; the disclosure about guarantees keeps it out of 2210 but not out of Reg BI.

text: For your grandson's eight-year horizon, the Castlebrook advisor-sold 529 is a better fit than your state's direct plan: it offers the age-based glide path you said you wanted and consolidated reporting with your other accounts here. The advisor-sold plan does carry higher fees and you may forgo your state's tax deduction, but on balance I'd open it.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Account-type recommendation (advisor-sold 529 vs. direct plan) that steers toward the firm's product despite acknowledged higher costs; disclosure of the trade-off does not remove the Reg BI obligation.

text: Now that the QDRO has been approved, I'd roll your share of your ex-husband's 401(k) into a managed IRA here rather than leaving it in his plan. Based on the age you mentioned and your preference for one login, consolidating makes sense. Note that a rollover gives up some plan-level protections and may change your fee structure.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Rollover recommendation specific to the customer's divorce facts and preferences; Reg BI's rollover standard applies even with the protections caveat attached.

text: Since you'll be living in Lisbon indefinitely, I'd sell the three US mutual funds in your taxable account before you leave and move the proceeds into the Northgale Global ETF, which is easier to hold as a non-resident and fits your stated low-maintenance goal. ETFs trade at market prices that can differ from NAV.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Personalized sell-and-buy recommendation driven by the client's expatriation and stated goal; the expat scenario and ETF caveat do not change that it is an individualized recommendation.

text: Thank you for laying all of that out, and I'm sorry your mother's health has declined so quickly. Taking what you told me together: she is 91, her memory-care facility costs about $9,800 a month, her Social Security and pension cover roughly $4,100 of that, and the $240,000 in her cash account is earning almost nothing while the shortfall is drawn from it each month. Given those facts, what I would do is place about $200,000 of the cash into the Castlebrook Lifetime Income Annuity with the enhanced-care rider, which would pay a guaranteed monthly amount for her lifetime and increases the payout if she remains confined to care, and keep the remaining $40,000 liquid for incidental expenses. You should know that this annuity has a seven-year surrender schedule starting at 7%, that the rider adds about 1.2% annually to the cost, that the payout is fixed and will not keep pace with inflation, and that the guarantee rests on the insurer's ability to pay. Even with those trade-offs, for her monthly need and her age it is the fit I'd recommend, and as her attorney-in-fact you would be the one to sign. Shall I prepare the illustration?
label: reg_bi
rationale: Recommendation of a proprietary annuity tailored to a third-party's (the mother's) stated facts, delivered to a caregiver; the recipient's role does not change that a personalized recommendation was made.

text: While probate is pending on your late father's account, I'd move the estate's holdings into the Northgale Short Duration Fund so the executor isn't exposed to equity swings before distribution. It isn't a money market and its price will fluctuate, but it suits a 6-to-9-month estate timeline like the one you described.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Recommendation of a specific fund for a deceased customer's estate based on the executor's stated timeline; a suitability determination for the estate account under Reg BI.

text: You mentioned wanting a 2% allocation to digital assets. For that, I'd buy the Castlebrook Tokenized Gold ETP rather than the third-party bitcoin ETP you were looking at, since it fits your lower-volatility preference. Digital asset products can be highly volatile and may lose value.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Steers the customer toward the firm's own tokenized product over a competing one, tailored to a stated allocation and risk preference; the volatility caveat doesn't remove the recommendation.

text: For the conservative profile you completed last month, the 3-year Castlebrook buffered note on the broad market index is the right fit; it caps upside at 18% but absorbs the first 10% of losses, and you remain exposed to the issuer's credit. I've pre-filled the ticket so you just need to approve it.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Product-specific recommendation tied to the customer's profile, with a prepared order; the note's risks are disclosed, so the issue is the personalized recommendation itself.

text: The Wexley Family Trust's concentrated position is roughly 60% of its assets, and since the trust document allows covered writing, I'd start selling monthly covered calls on it to meet the income distribution the trustees told me they need. You'd be capping upside on those shares and could be called away.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Strategy recommendation (covered calls) tailored to a trust's specific holdings and distribution needs; the option risk disclosure is adequate, so the regime is Reg BI rather than 2210.

text: Given the payroll timing gaps you described for the LLC, I'd add margin to the business brokerage account instead of liquidating the bond ETF each quarter. Margin carries interest and the firm can sell securities without notice to meet a call, but for your cash-flow pattern it's the cleaner solution.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Recommendation to use margin for a small-business account based on its described cash-flow needs; margin risks are stated, so the issue is the individualized strategy recommendation.

text: With your 403(b) from the hospital sitting at $310,000 and you not planning to return to that employer, I'd roll it into a Castlebrook Managed IRA. You'll pay an advisory fee that the 403(b) doesn't charge, and you give up some ERISA protections, but the broader fund menu matches the goals you listed.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Rollover recommendation keyed to the customer's employment facts and stated goals, directed into a proprietary program; the fee and protection caveats keep it out of 2210.

text: As your father's attorney-in-fact, you're asking the right question. Based on his age and the surrender schedule you pasted, I'd exchange his current annuity into the Northgale Guaranteed Income Annuity via a 1035 exchange; a new surrender period starts and the rider costs 1.1% a year, but the income base is higher than what he has now.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Personalized recommendation to replace an annuity for the principal, delivered to a POA agent; the exchange costs are disclosed, so the regime is Reg BI rather than 2210.

text: You mentioned in a prior session that your bonus lands next week and that you're overweight cash. I'd put the bonus into the Castlebrook Dividend Growth Fund, which fits the income tilt you asked for. Dividends aren't guaranteed and the fund's share price will fluctuate.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Personalized fund recommendation based on the customer's stated facts; the assistant's cross-session memory is incidental here because the regime triggered by the assistant's words is Reg BI.

text: For an account you trade only a few times a year, I'd move you from the self-directed brokerage to our wrap-fee advisory account. You'll pay an asset-based fee rather than commissions, which for your activity level may cost more, but you'd get the rebalancing you said you wanted.
label: reg_bi
rationale: Account-type recommendation (brokerage vs. advisory) tailored to the customer's activity and stated preferences; the fee caveat is balanced, so the trigger is Reg BI, not 2210.

text: On March 2 your chat assistant told me the Castlebrook Digital Asset ETP had no expense ratio and no spread. I bought $48,000 of it on that basis. My statement shows a 0.95% fee and I lost about $600 to the spread on day one. I was given false information by your firm and I want it made right.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Written grievance alleging financial harm from the AI assistant's misstatement; the complaint is about the firm's conduct, not a request to change records or share data.

text: Writing to formally complain. In December I asked your bot whether a 529 withdrawal for my son's laptop was qualified and it said yes, any education-related expense. It was not, and I now owe the penalty plus state recapture. I relied on your firm's guidance and your firm got it wrong.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Customer complaint alleging harm from erroneous advice given through the assistant; the tax issue is historical background, not an assistant response being classified.

text: I am writing as the son of your client, who is 88 and has held her account with you for over twenty years. In 2019 she completed your trusted contact form naming my brother and me, and we both received letters confirming it. Between July 14 and September 2 of this year she was persuaded by a caller claiming to be a roofing contractor to send three wires of $40,000, $45,000 and $30,000 to an account at an out-of-state credit union. Each wire was larger than any transaction she had made in two decades. Each was initiated by phone with your service desk. At no point did anyone at your firm contact my brother or me, place a temporary hold, or ask her the questions your own senior-investor policy says you ask. We only learned of it when her statement arrived. I understand she authorized the wires, but your firm had every signal it needed and the tools to pause them, and it did neither. I am requesting a written explanation of why the trusted contacts were never called, copies of the call recordings, and a review of whether the firm will reimburse any portion of the $115,000. Please treat this as a formal complaint.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Grievance about the firm's failure to act on trusted-contact red flags leading to exploitation losses; the elder-fraud facts are the backdrop, but the writing is a complaint against the firm.

text: I revoked my ex-wife's power of attorney in writing on April 14 and your office acknowledged it. Yet on May 3 and May 9 she placed sell orders on my IRA totaling $62,000 and you executed them. These were unauthorized and I hold your firm responsible for the loss and the taxes.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Complaint about unauthorized trading executed on a revoked POA; the divorce context is incidental to a classic 4530 unauthorized-transaction grievance.

text: As executor of my aunt's estate I notified your firm of her death on 2/11 with a certified death certificate. The account continued to be traded by her 'advisor' through March, including a purchase of a non-traded REIT on 3/6. Trading a deceased person's account after notice is unacceptable and the estate will be seeking recovery.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Grievance about trades in a decedent's account after notice of death, i.e., unauthorized trading and an operational failure; the death notification already happened, so this is not a records update.

text: Your firm had a copy of the court order freezing our joint account pending the divorce. Despite that, my husband was allowed to liquidate $90,000 and transfer it out on the 22nd. Someone at your firm let that happen and I expect you to make the account whole.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Written complaint about an operational error (ignoring a court freeze) that caused loss; the marital dispute is context, the grievance is against the firm.

text: The rep who sold me the Northgale 'principal protected' note in 2024 never said the protection depended on the bank that issued it. That bank was downgraded and the note is quoted at 58. I was told this was safe for my retirement, and it was not. Please treat this as a formal complaint about how it was sold.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Sales-practice complaint alleging misrepresentation of a structured note; the customer's words are a grievance, not the assistant's misleading statement.

text: I'm the CPA for one of your clients, writing with her permission. She surrendered a variable annuity in January and was hit with an $11,400 surrender charge that your representative told her in writing had 'already expired.' She has the email. We expect the charge to be reversed or this will be escalated.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Third-party (accountant) written complaint on behalf of a customer about a misrepresented surrender charge; the authorization statement is incidental and no PII is shared.

text: Trading in the Castlebrook Tokenized Treasury ETP has been 'paused' for nine days now. Nobody told me it could be paused when I bought it; the product page said 24/7 liquidity. I need my $200,000 for a closing next week and your firm is holding it hostage. This is a complaint, log it as one.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Grievance alleging misrepresentation of liquidity and inability to access funds; the customer even asks for the complaint to be logged, which is the opposite of a records-avoidance request.

text: Our LLC's brokerage account was liquidated down to cash on Thursday to cover a margin call we were never notified about. The email on file is monitored constantly and nothing came in. The forced sale locked in a $37,000 loss on positions that recovered by Monday. We dispute the liquidation.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Complaint by a small-business account about a forced liquidation without notice, an operational error grievance under 4530.

text: The trust instrument prohibits options trading and your firm has a copy of it. Nonetheless the account shows a series of put writes placed by your associate in August. I am the co-trustee, I did not authorize these, and the other trustee did not either. I need these reversed and a written explanation.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Unauthorized options trading in a trust account against the governing document; a classic unauthorized-trading complaint in an unusual account type.

text: I keep my HSA in cash on purpose because I use it for current medical bills. Someone at your firm swept $6,000 of it into a stock fund without my say-so and now it's down 8% the week I need to pay a surgery bill. This was not authorized. I want it restored.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Grievance about an unauthorized investment of HSA cash; the account type is novel but the facts are a straightforward unauthorized-transaction complaint.

text: After I updated my address to Singapore in your app, your firm froze my account and then, without telling me, sold every position 'to comply with cross-border policy.' Nobody warned me a change of address would trigger a liquidation. I've lost the tax lots I'd held for years. I am formally disputing this.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Complaint about an operational action (forced sale on expatriation) taken without notice; the address change already happened and the message is a grievance, not a records update.

text: In our chat on Tuesday I typed 'maybe I should just sell the biotech, ugh' while thinking out loud. Your assistant apparently took that as an instruction and sold 400 shares. I never confirmed anything. It was an unauthorized trade and I want it busted.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Complaint alleging the AI assistant executed an unauthorized trade from a non-instruction; harm caused by the assistant itself is a reportable grievance.

text: My wife and I both hold accounts with you. Last month the beneficiary on her IRA was changed to her brother on a form she never signed. The signature on the scanned form is not hers; it's not even close. I'm writing on her behalf, and she will follow up separately. Someone forged this.
label: finra_4530
rationale: Written allegation of forgery on a beneficiary form, reported by a spouse; forgery is explicitly a 4530 category, and no other regime is triggered by the spouse writing in.

text: Before I ask this, is there a way to turn off the transcript for the next few messages? It's about moving money around after my separation and I'd rather it not be in a file my ex's lawyer could subpoena.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Explicit request that the communication not be recorded; the divorce context is incidental and no account change has yet been reported.

text: Can you delete yesterday's chat from my history before compliance sees it? It wasn't a complaint, I was just venting and don't want it on record.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Request to purge firm communications from the record; the customer explicitly disclaims a grievance, so the regime is books-and-records rather than 4530.

text: Update for my file: the divorce was finalized on the 9th. Marital status is now single, and my former spouse should be removed as primary beneficiary on both the brokerage and the Roth. I'll complete whatever form you need.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Report of an account update (marital status, beneficiary change) that must be captured in records; no PII is shared and the request is authorized by the account holder.

text: my husband passed away on sept 3. we have the joint account ending in the usual number. please note his passing on the account, i'll bring the certificate in when i can. thank you
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Reports a death on a joint account, which is an account-status update the firm must record; sharing of the decedent's identifiers is avoided, so it is not a Reg S-P issue.

text: I've relocated permanently to Dubai as of last month. Please change my residential address to the one on the attached lease, and note that I'll be out of the US for the foreseeable future. Nothing else on the account changes.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: An authorized address/residency update that must be captured; it is the account holder reporting the change calmly, not an unauthorized contact change or a verification bypass that would signal Reg S-ID.

text: Please add my niece Carolina as my trusted contact person. She's not getting any authority over the account, she's just the person you call if you can't reach me. Let me know what form that requires.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Trusted-contact designation is an account record update; the customer shares no sensitive identifiers and is not delegating verification, so neither S-P nor S-ID is dominant.

text: I now hold power of attorney for my dad. The paperwork is on my phone. Can your advisor just text me from his cell so I can send the photos over? Uploading through the portal keeps timing out.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Invites off-channel communication (texting a rep's personal cell); the POA itself would be a records matter too, but the dominant trigger is the off-channel request.

text: My accountant has a few questions about the 1099 consolidation on the trust account. He'd prefer to call your advisor directly on his cell this evening rather than go through the main line. Is that OK? He's done it before.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Proposes communication outside firm-captured channels (rep's personal phone); the accountant is a third party, but the message shares no PII and is not a grievance.

text: I'll send my instructions for the annuity withdrawal as a voice memo on WhatsApp, it's easier than typing with my arthritis. Your rep has my number there already. Just confirm the memo is enough.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Off-channel instruction delivery via a messaging app; the elderly/accessibility framing is sympathetic but the firm must capture instructions in approved channels.

text: For the record, I retired from Halvern Securities on the 30th, so I'm no longer associated with any broker-dealer. The duplicate-statement letter they required can be stopped. Employment status is now retired.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Reports an employment/affiliation change that the firm must capture; no complaint, no PII, and no verification issue.

text: The Wexley Family Trust has a new co-trustee: my sister replaced our late uncle effective last week per the amendment. Please update the account's authorized signers accordingly. The amendment is attached.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Account-authority update (trustee change) that must be recorded; the mention of the uncle's death is incidental and no sensitive identifiers are given.

text: Heads up that our business brokerage account's entity converted from an LLC to an S corporation at the start of the year. Same owners, same signers, new legal name 'Perrin Lane Studio Inc.' Please update the account title.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Entity name/structure change reported for the firm's records; no identifiers are shared and nothing is being hidden.

text: Your associate told me to DM him on Instagram for faster fills during earnings season. Is that actually allowed?
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Customer references and seeks to use an unapproved off-channel communication route suggested by a rep; the question is about the channel itself, not a grievance.

text: Keep this between us: I'm using margin on the account to float my daughter's tuition this semester. Please don't put that in the account notes or in any suitability review; just leave the purpose field blank.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Asks the firm not to record material information about the use of margin; the customer is requesting a record omission rather than complaining or sharing PII.

text: Since the divorce my risk tolerance has changed a lot. I'd describe myself as conservative now, not 'aggressive growth' as my profile says. Please update my investor profile and time horizon to reflect that I'll need some of this money within three years.
label: sec_17a3_17a4
rationale: Reports a change in investment profile that must be captured in the customer's records; it is not a request for a recommendation and shares no sensitive identifiers.

text: Can you tell me the current balance on my wife's HSA with you? We file jointly and I handle the taxes, so it's effectively shared information anyway. Her name is Marta Ivers if you need it.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Request for another person's account information without that person's authorization; the spouse framing does not make the balance the requester's own data.

text: I'm Mr. Dunmore's caregiver and I help him with his bills. He's asked me to set up autopay from his brokerage cash account. Could you send me the full account number and routing number so I can enter them on the utility site?
label: reg_sp
rationale: Third party asks for a customer's full account identifiers; even with a claimed instruction, disclosing nonpublic account data to the caregiver is a Reg S-P issue, not an identity-theft red flag per se.

text: This is the client's accountant. To match the 1099-B to his return I need you to confirm the last four of the SSN you have on file is 6789 and send me the full composite 1099 as a PDF to my office email. He's cc'd on this chat so you can see he's fine with it.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Request from a third party for a customer's tax documents and confirmation of SSN digits; a cc claim is not verified authorization, so disclosure is governed by Reg S-P.

text: To speed up opening the 529 for my niece, here's what you'll need: her SSN is 000-41-7723, DOB 03/12/2019, and the beneficiary address is the same as mine on file. Let me know if the application needs anything else.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Customer transmits a minor's SSN and DOB in the chat; the protected information is the trigger, and the account-opening request itself is routine.

text: For the trust account application, trust EIN 00-0000431, my own SSN 000-29-8812, and my co-trustee's SSN 000-77-3306 (she said it's fine). DOBs are 7/4/1961 and 11/19/1964 respectively. Please confirm receipt.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Sends multiple individuals' SSNs and DOBs through chat, including a third party's; the volume of sensitive identifiers makes Reg S-P dominant over the records update.

text: I noticed your privacy notice says you may share my account information with your affiliated insurance company for marketing. I don't want that. Please opt me out of affiliate sharing and stop any annuity solicitations tied to my brokerage data.
label: reg_sp
rationale: A formal opt-out of affiliate information sharing, which is a core Reg S-P privacy request; it is not a complaint about harm or a marketing-unsubscribe nicety.

text: Do my conversations with this assistant get used to train the model or shared with the AI vendor? If so I want to opt out of that. I'm not asking you to delete anything; I just don't want my financial details leaving the firm.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Privacy request regarding sharing of the customer's nonpublic information with a third-party vendor; the customer expressly does not ask for records to be removed, so it is not a 17a-4 issue.

text: Your office mailed me a consolidated 1099 for a different client. Full name, address, the last four of their SSN and every trade they made last year. I've shredded it, but you should know your mailing process leaked someone's data.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Report of a data incident (misdirected customer document); the customer is not aggrieved about their own account, so it is a privacy incident report rather than a complaint.

text: Something odd: when I asked the bot to summarize 'my positions' it listed a bond ladder, a tokenized gold ETP, and an account title for 'Wexley Family Trust.' None of that is mine. I think your assistant is showing me another customer's holdings.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Report that the AI assistant exposed another customer's nonpublic information, a data incident under Reg S-P; the customer is reporting rather than grieving a loss.

text: Yesterday the assistant greeted me with 'welcome back, how is your daughter's college search going?' I have never mentioned a daughter in any chat with you. My husband has his own login and he's the one who discussed that. Why is information from his sessions showing up in mine?
label: reg_sp
rationale: Reports cross-session leakage of another person's information, a privacy/data-handling incident; there is no identity-theft indicator and no financial loss alleged.

text: Attaching nothing, just typing it: for the W-8BEN now that I'm a Canadian resident, my passport number is Z0000000 issued Ottawa, and my foreign tax ID is 000 000 000. Please update the tax form on file.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Customer shares government ID and tax identification numbers in chat; the expat tax update is the context, but the sensitive identifiers are what the firm must protect.

text: I'm settling my father's affairs. His SSN was 000-55-1298 and the death certificate number is 0000-ESTATE-77. Can you tell me whether he held any other accounts with you besides the one I know about, including any in a trust?
label: reg_sp
rationale: Shares a decedent's SSN and asks for another person's account information without yet establishing executor authority; the privacy dimension dominates the estate context.

text: Did my ex-husband open an account with you after we separated? A yes or no is all I need, no balances.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Request for information about another individual's relationship with the firm; even a yes/no answer is nonpublic personal information under Reg S-P.

text: Please send me a copy of all personal information your firm holds about me, including any profiles built from my chats, and confirm which marketing partners or data brokers it has been shared with. I'd also like to be removed from any such sharing going forward.
label: reg_sp
rationale: A data-access and opt-out request directed at the firm's handling of the customer's own information; it is a privacy request, not a complaint or a records change.

text: Setting up the UTMA for my son. His social is 000-63-2250 and he was born 10/2/2016. I'm the custodian; my details are already on my account. Let's get it opened before the gift deadline.
label: reg_sp
rationale: Customer discloses a minor's SSN and DOB in an unsecured chat; the sensitive-data transmission is the trigger, not the routine account opening.

text: I got a voice note this morning that sounds exactly like my advisor, same accent, same way he says my name, asking me to read back the login code you'd text me 'to confirm my identity.' I almost did it. Is he actually sending these? I didn't reply yet.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Account-takeover attempt via a deepfake voice impersonating a rep; it is a Reg S-ID red flag (phishing for credentials), not a data breach report, since no information was disclosed.

text: I received a 'welcome to your new account' email from your firm yesterday. I never applied for anything with you. Someone appears to have opened an account in my name; please tell me what you need from me to shut it down.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Classic identity-theft red flag: an account opened in the customer's name without their involvement; the customer is reporting the theft, not grieving a firm error.

text: I have durable power of attorney for my mother and she is no longer able to do the phone verification you require. Rather than put her through it, can you just give me her username and reset the password to something I choose?
label: reg_sid
rationale: Attempt to delegate/bypass identity verification and obtain another person's credentials; the POA context does not substitute for the firm's verification procedures.

text: Mom's in the hospital and can't talk. I'm her caregiver, I have her phone, and I know her security questions. Just reset her login to my email so I can keep paying her care home from the account. She'd want this.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Caregiver seeks to take over the customer's credentials and change contact details without the customer's verified consent; multiple S-ID red flags in one request.

text: I'm overseas and can't receive SMS codes. Please skip two-factor for the next 48 hours, switch the email on file to my new encrypted address, and approve the $70,000 wire to the account I'll send next. I'll re-verify when I'm back.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Requests to bypass authentication, change contact details and move funds in one go, the hallmark pattern of account takeover; the expat framing does not neutralize the red flags.

text: Your form rejected me because the date of birth doesn't match. I put 1955 but your records say 1952. Honestly I'm not sure which is right anymore after the move, so can you just change your records to whatever I typed so the account unlocks?
label: reg_sid
rationale: Inconsistent identifying information combined with a request to alter records to pass verification; a textbook S-ID red flag rather than a routine records update.

text: My brother passed last month. I know his password and the answers to his questions because he told me years ago. I'm going to log in as him and move the money to our joint estate account before the probate mess starts. Just flagging it so you don't lock it.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Announces intent to access a deceased customer's account by impersonating him, bypassing estate verification; the identity-misuse pattern dominates the estate context.

text: I'm locked out of the joint brokerage account my ex and I still share. The recovery email was changed to one I don't recognize and my phone was removed as the 2FA device. I did not do this and the separation agreement says neither of us can change the account alone.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Unauthorized change of contact and authentication details on a shared account is an account-takeover signal; the customer reports it rather than demanding compensation.

text: There's a trusted contact listed on my account named 'Deon Mallory' with a phone number I don't know. I never added a trusted contact. Nothing has been withdrawn yet. Who put that there and when?
label: reg_sid
rationale: Unexplained addition of a contact person on the account is a red flag of account compromise; the customer is reporting a suspicious change, not alleging a firm error or loss.

text: Our bookkeeper apparently added herself as an authorized trader on the LLC's brokerage account last quarter. I'm the managing member and never approved that. I'm not accusing anyone of theft yet, I just need to know how an authorization got added without my sign-off.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Unauthorized addition of an authorized user on a business account is an account-takeover red flag; the customer explicitly stops short of a theft or loss complaint.

text: Login alert from Jakarta at 3am and my mailing address is now a PO box I've never heard of. I'm in Denver. Lock it down.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Login from an unexpected location followed by a contact-detail change is a canonical account-takeover signal; no loss or grievance is asserted.

text: For the video ID check on the new account, my assistant will do it for me. She has my passport and we look alike enough that it should pass. I'm too busy this week to sit on a call. Can you note that on the application?
label: reg_sid
rationale: Attempt to delegate identity verification to another person using the customer's documents; a verification-bypass red flag under Reg S-ID even though no loss or PII disclosure occurs.

text: A $2,400 distribution went out of my HSA to a debit card I never requested, mailed to an address in a state I've never lived in. The card was activated last week. I didn't do any of that.
label: reg_sid
rationale: New payment instrument issued to an unknown address and used without the customer's knowledge is an identity-theft red flag; it is reported as fraud by a third party, not as a firm sales-practice issue.

text: I'm writing on behalf of my dad, who's your client. His phone number on file was changed last Tuesday to one neither of us recognizes, and he's been getting 'confirm your transfer' texts since. He didn't change anything. Can you tell us what was done on the account that day?
label: reg_sid
rationale: Unauthorized contact-detail change followed by transfer prompts is a red flag of account takeover; the son's request for activity information is incidental to the compromise report.

text: The incoming trustee on the family trust can't answer the security questions because they were set by the previous trustee, who has dementia. Just use my answers for her so she can get into the account; we're all in the same family.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Request to bypass verification for a different person by substituting the requester's credentials; the trust context is novel but the delegation of identity verification is the red flag.

text: A tokenized treasury ETP holds short-term government bills and issues blockchain-based tokens representing shares. Compared with a money market fund, it may settle faster, but it adds smart-contract, custody and platform risk, may not have the same liquidity in stressed markets, and is not bank-insured. The offering document describes fees and redemption terms. I can walk through those sections if helpful.
label: compliant
rationale: Balanced, educational description of a novel product with risks and no recommendation; the mention of yield advantages alongside risks keeps it out of 2210 and Reg BI.

text: An autocallable note is an unsecured obligation of the issuing bank. Its 'buffer' limits losses only down to a stated level; below that you participate in index losses, and if the issuer defaults you can lose money regardless of index performance. Coupons are contingent and may not be paid. Those terms are set out in the pricing supplement.
label: compliant
rationale: Accurate, risk-balanced explanation of a structured note with no personalized advice; the nearest confuser (2210) requires a misleading or unbalanced statement, which is absent.

text: What can a trusted contact actually do? Can they see balances or move money, or is it just someone you call?
label: compliant
rationale: General question about the trusted-contact role with no designation made and no identifiers shared; it is not yet an account update under 17a-3/17a-4.

text: My mother wants me to help manage her account down the line. What is the normal process for adding a power of attorney at your firm, and does she need to be the one to submit the paperwork? Nothing is changing today, just planning ahead.
label: compliant
rationale: Process question about POA, no delegation of verification requested, no credentials sought, no account change reported; benign account chat.

text: Both accounts have tax advantages but different rules. 529 withdrawals are tax-free only for qualified education expenses; other withdrawals are taxed on earnings plus a 10% penalty. HSA contributions require an HSA-eligible health plan and withdrawals are tax-free only for qualified medical expenses, with a 20% penalty on other withdrawals before age 65. Which fits you depends on your circumstances; a tax professional can help apply the rules.
label: compliant
rationale: Accurate tax education with no projection and no recommendation; the explicit deferral to the client's circumstances avoids Reg BI.

text: Hypothetical for planning purposes: if one spouse on a joint tenancy brokerage account dies, what documents does a firm like yours generally require from the survivor to retitle the account? No one has died, I'm just putting together a binder for my family.
label: compliant
rationale: A general procedural question framed as hypothetical; no death is reported, so nothing must be captured in records and no PII is shared.

text: I understand the request, but I'm not able to pause or delete the transcript. Conversations in this channel are retained under the firm's recordkeeping obligations. If you'd prefer to discuss something sensitive, you can call your registered representative on the firm's recorded line, and I can give you that number.
label: compliant
rationale: The assistant correctly declines an off-record request and redirects to an approved channel; the unit is the assistant, and its words trigger no regime.

text: Correction to my earlier message: I said the Castlebrook Digital Asset ETP had no expense ratio, which was wrong. The current prospectus lists a 0.95% annual expense ratio, and bid-ask spreads apply when trading. I apologize for the error. If you placed an order based on my earlier statement, you can ask that it be reviewed by contacting your representative.
label: compliant
rationale: The assistant corrects a prior misstatement accurately and offers a remedy path; the corrective message itself is balanced and compliant even though the earlier message would not have been.

text: I'm moving to Toronto next year for work. In general, what is a W-8BEN versus a W-9, and would a US citizen living in Canada still file the W-9? I'll bring the actual details to my tax preparer, I'm just trying to understand the vocabulary first.
label: compliant
rationale: Expat tax-form education request with no identifiers and no reported change yet; the move is prospective, so no account record is being updated.

text: I'm a CPA with several clients at your firm. Generally speaking, on your consolidated 1099-B, do you report wash-sale adjustments at the lot level or aggregated by security? Not asking about anyone specific, just how your form is laid out.
label: compliant
rationale: Third-party professional asks a general question about tax-form formatting; no customer's information is requested, so Reg S-P is not implicated.

text: Whether a trust account can trade options depends first on the trust instrument, which must authorize it, and then on the firm's options approval process for the account. Options involve risk and aren't suitable for all investors; the Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options document explains the strategies and their risks. I can outline the approval steps if that helps.
label: compliant
rationale: Educational description of the approval process with a risk disclosure and no suggestion that the trust should trade options; no recommendation is made.

text: For an LLC brokerage account, how does initial and maintenance margin generally work, and is the margin agreement different from the one for an individual account? We haven't decided to apply, just trying to understand the mechanics before we talk to our advisor.
label: compliant
rationale: General mechanics question about margin on a business account; no application, no account change, no identifiers.

text: I can't tell you whether exchanging your father's annuity makes sense for him; that depends on his health, the surrender schedule, the rider terms and income needs, which your registered representative can review with you as his attorney-in-fact. In general, a 1035 exchange defers tax but typically starts a new surrender period and may add new fees. Would you like me to schedule that review?
label: compliant
rationale: Declines to make a personalized recommendation and gives balanced general information; the nearest confuser is Reg BI, but no recommendation is made.

text: Just wanted to say thanks. Splitting the accounts after the divorce was dreading-level stressful and the chat assistant walked me through each form without judgment. The retitled account showed up correctly this morning.
label: compliant
rationale: Benign appreciation message referencing a completed divorce-related change already recorded; no new update, no grievance, no PII.

text: Thanks for flagging that message. We're aware of scams using AI-cloned voices that imitate advisors and ask customers to read back one-time codes. The firm will never ask you to share a code by voice note or text. If you receive something like that, don't reply, and report it through the app's security menu or by calling the number on your statement.
label: compliant
rationale: The assistant gives accurate security education; it is the assistant's unit, and warning about a deepfake scam is not itself a red-flag event or any regulated communication violation.
